transcript:
Header: 2025-02-14 16:00 PST | Duration 49m | Recorded on Fireflies
Attendees: Sarah Kim (Redwood AE), Mateo Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Head of MLOps, MeduCo), Tom Reynolds (Platform Eng), Dr. Lena Vogel (Data Privacy Officer), Carlos Mendes (CTO), Jin Park (Security)

Summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete): talk about on-prem air gap, model updates via physical media, signed images, required FIPS compliance; next steps agreed.

00:00 Sarah Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. quick intro from our side, I'm Sarah, AE at Redwood, with Mateo, our solutions engineer. we wanted to get a sense of your constraints for the air-gapped deployment.
00:12 Priya Shah: Hi Sarah, yeah we're sort of in inference procurement mode, two things drive this: PHI handling and our regulators require no outbound connections from the inference clusters. so internet disabled, no SaaS callbacks.
00:25 Tom Reynolds: we also have limited rack space and an existing vault HSM for key management. power budget is pretty tight in our datacenter pods — 11kW per rack is our practical ceiling.
00:38 Mateo Alvarez: okay that's helpful. just to confirm — by air-gapped you mean zero egress, no periodic internet connections even for metrics or heartbeats?
00:44 Jin Park: correct, strictly no egress. we can have an internal telemetry aggregator but it can't reach the internet.
00:52 Sarah Kim: got it. Redwood Private supports fully disconnected installs with a customer-managed control plane. Mateo, do you want to walk through how we package the runtime and models for offline installs?
01:03 Mateo Alvarez: sure — high level, we produce signed container images and a set of signed model artifacts. customers import those via USB or secure NFS over an internal transfer process. we also provide a one-time bootstrap bundle that includes the management UI and the local control plane components. for patches and new model versions, we issue psu-style signed updates.
01:23 Priya Shah: psu-style? like how firmware updates are signed?
01:27 Mateo Alvarez: yeah exactly. images are cryptographically signed with Redwood's release key and can be verified against your local root of trust. we also support bringing your own signing key (BYOK) using your HSM.
01:37 Dr. Lena Vogel: bringing our own key is mandatory for the DPA in our space. we can't rely on vendor-owned signing keys. how does rotation work offline?
01:45 Mateo Alvarez: rotation is an offline process. we provide tooling to generate a rotation bundle that you sign in your HSM and then import. it's a manual step but auditable — logs are kept locally, and you can export the signed events for audits.
01:57 Tom Reynolds: what's the runtime footprint? our current plan has 2 x A100s per node but the data sheet suggests H100s for some of the large models. procurement lead times for H100s are months right now.
02:12 Mateo Alvarez: footprint depends on model and quantization. for standard Llama-family 13B quantized to int8 you can run on A100 with ~40GB memory profile; H100s give better perf for 70B+ models. we can produce a profile table after you share target models and expected qps/latency.
02:28 Carlos Mendes: our initial scope is 1-2M inference tokens per day, mostly short prompts for triage classification — latency SLO is 300ms p50, 800ms p95. is that realistic on A100?
02:40 Mateo Alvarez: for short seqs and smaller models, yes, you can meet those SLOs. for heavier sequences we'd recommend batching or move to H100. we'll include sample bench numbers in the sizing doc.
02:49 Priya Shah: second big constraint: no automatic callbacks for telemetry. how does Redwood handle health checks and crash reporting in air-gapped mode? we need to ensure we can still get actionable logs without exfil.
02:59 Sarah Kim: we ship a local telemetry collector that writes to your internal SIEM/ELK. in air-gapped installs, you keep the metrics internal. Redwood's support access is via a temporary, customer-controlled bastion step — you can create a time-limited support bundle if you permit it, otherwise we work from logs you share out-of-band.
03:18 Jin Park: temporary bastion — we need to see the flow; our policy requires MFA and explicit approval per session.
03:24 Sarah Kim: that's standard. the support flow is human-in-the-loop: you're in control.
03:29 Dr. Lena Vogel: auditability is essential. we need tamper-evident transfer logs for any model updates. can you store transfer manifests locally with a chain of custody?
03:37 Mateo Alvarez: yes, each update bundle contains a manifest and a cryptographic signature. the runtime verifies signatures before loading. manifests include SHA256 checksums and a transfer metadata header you can pipe into your audit system.
03:48 Tom Reynolds: on practicalities — do you require a special OS or runtime? we prefer RHEL 8.6, and our infra team will only accept signed RPMs for kernel modules.
03:58 Mateo Alvarez: Redwood runtime is distributed as signed containers and an agent. we support RHEL and Ubuntu. kernel modules aren't required except for some NVidia driver variants; we ship validated driver versions and signed module instructions.
04:09 Priya Shah: patching cadence — we can't do weekly model updates due to change control. our cadence is quarterly model pushes with emergency patches as exception. how do you support delayed rollout?
04:19 Mateo Alvarez: our rollout policy supports staged imports and pinning. you can import multiple versions to a staging namespace and then promote on your cadence. emergency patches are signed and you decide whether to apply.
04:28 Carlos Mendes: what's the support SLA for on-prem air-gapped customers? we need a commercial SLA — uptime and response times.
04:34 Sarah Kim: for Private customers we offer enterprise SLAs as an add-on; response times and on-call 24/7 are possible under a dedicated contract. we'll include options in the pricing doc.
04:44 Tom Reynolds: another constraint — our hardware vendor only supports certain BIOS versions and secure boot. do you validate on specific node images?
04:50 Mateo Alvarez: we publish recommended images and secure boot guidelines. the deployment script supports secure boot and will verify signatures at startup. we can also produce a checklist for your procurement team.
05:03 Priya Shah: regulatory Qs: SOC2 and ISO are baseline. do you have FIPS-certified crypto paths for the key material?
05:10 Sarah Kim: Redwood's cloud has SOC2 and ISO artifacts; for on-prem we provide guidance. FIPS level crypto is supported if you use your HSM and configure the runtime to use FIPS TLS stacks. we'll share our FIPS notes and required configuration.
05:22 Jin Park: what about model provenance? we need to know exactly which model weights and tokenizers are in each bundle for compliance.
05:30 Mateo Alvarez: manifests include model name, hash, tokenizer version, and a model provenance tag. we also support attaching a signed prompt evaluation artifact so you can reproduce quality checks.
05:41 Tom Reynolds: are there limitations around quantization libraries in air-gapped mode — e.g., do you need internet for extra wheels or compiled kernels?
05:48 Mateo Alvarez: no internet required at runtime. any specialized kernels are provided in the signed install bundle for your architecture. if you need vendor-specific kernels (e.g., Ampere or Hopper optimized kernels), we include them or provide instructions to build offline; we can also precompile for you.
05:59 Priya Shah: licensing model — do we need a perpetual license for on-prem or is it subscription? we need clear renewal terms for budgeting.
06:07 Sarah Kim: Private deployments are subscription-based with either annual or multi-year contracts; there are also options for reserved capacity licensing if you commit to GPU counts. we'll include pricing tiers in the follow-up.
06:16 Carlos Mendes: curious about offline inference accuracy drift monitoring — can Redwood run evals locally against a baseline prompt set and produce a report?
06:24 Mateo Alvarez: yes, we support local eval harnesses; you can run periodic offline regressions and store the report locally. we can also help bootstrap the baseline eval set.
06:32 Dr. Lena Vogel: any recollection of previous incidents in air-gapped installs — supply chain or image tampering? how does Redwood mitigate?
06:39 Sarah Kim: mitigation is layered: signed artifacts, BYOK, HSM attestations, and verified manifests. we also recommend a hardened import pipeline — quarantine, scan, and then deploy. we'll share recommended SOPs.
06:52 Tom Reynolds: network architecture: we'd like to run inference in a segmented network zone, with no outbound NAT. is that supported?
06:58 Mateo Alvarez: yes — the runtime can be deployed entirely within a segmented VLAN. only requirements are internal DNS and access to your internal blob store for model artifacts.
07:08 Priya Shah: can we have short lived debug endpoints that you can call into only over an encrypted direct link for high severity incidents?
07:14 Sarah Kim: yes that’s the temporary bastion model — we provide an ephemeral support ssh flow where you approve each session and it requires MFA.
07:21 Carlos Mendes: procurement Q — if we choose Redwood Private, do we still get model updates from upstream open model projects? we need clarity on who is responsible for model vulnerabilities.
07:31 Mateo Alvarez: Redwood does not modify upstream models unless you ask. we package community models and apply our own performance patches (e.g., kernel config). vulnerability notifications are provided; you control whether to accept the updated model bundle.
07:41 Jin Park: ok, one last: offline telemetry for usage-based billing — how do you reconcile usage if we're offline?
07:48 Sarah Kim: for on-prem we support an offline metering collector that you periodically export as a signed usage file and upload to our billing portal. we can also do fixed reserved capacity to avoid metering if that's simpler.
07:59 Priya Shah: thanks — useful. next steps?
08:03 Sarah Kim: recap: we will send the air-gap install guide, signing & BYOK flow, and recommended hardware configs. Mateo will create a sizing workbook. Priya, you will confirm maintenance windows and give target models. we'll also include SLA options and pricing.
08:14 Priya Shah: yes will do. thanks.

[End of transcript — rough auto-timestamps every ~30–90s. Note: transcription errors possible: "HSM" sometimes transcribed as "H S M" or "A 100" as "A one hundred" in some exports.]
